database_summary: Relational OLTP/analytical mix for a beer/distribution domain: core entities are products, product groups, breweries, customers, orders and inventory. Time-series facts include monthly_sales, purchases, ticker, web counters/visits and server heartbeats. Several dimension-like lookup tables (channels_dim, gender_dim, packaging). Some tables encode semi-structured lists (customer_favorites, customer_reviews). Many tables are small; primary keys are as declared in DDL. The schema contains history/event tables (purchases, monthly_sales, web_page_visits, web_counter_hist, ticker, server_heartbeat, emp_hire_periods, picking_log) and current-state tables (products, customers, inventory, locations, stock). Watch joins that can multiply rows: order -> orderlines, orders -> customers, products -> monthly_sales/purchases/inventory produce 1-to-many expansions. Several tables use composite primary keys (month+product, page+app+day) implying time-series grain.

accepted.name: products_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT p.id AS id,
       p.name AS name,
       p.group_id AS group_id,
       pg.name AS name_group,
       pa.sales_volume AS sales_volume,
       pa.abv AS abv
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN product_groups pg ON p.group_id = pg.id
LEFT JOIN product_alcohol pa ON p.id = pa.product_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-product dimension combining product core attributes with group and alcohol metadata. Useful to enrich sales, purchases, inventory, and orders with product name, group name, sales_volume and abv. | Use for: Look up product attributes for reporting or joins (name, group, alcohol).; Compute sales/purchase/inventory rollups enriched with product metadata.; Filter products by group name or abv ranges.

accepted.name: monthly_sales_agg_by_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT product_id AS product_id,
       mth AS mth,
       SUM(qty) AS qty_total
FROM monthly_sales
GROUP BY product_id, mth
accepted.description: Aggregated monthly sales measures per product and month. Produces one row per product_id+mth with total qty. Useful as a canonical sales fact for time-series analyses and comparisons to budgets. | Use for: Monthly time series of sales for products.; Compare monthly_sales to monthly_budget or compute growth rates.; Join to products_dim to get product names for reporting.

accepted.name: purchases_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT pur.id AS id,
       pur.purchased AS purchased,
       pur.brewery_id AS brewery_id,
       b.name AS name_brewery,
       pur.product_id AS product_id,
       p.name AS name_product,
       pur.qty AS qty,
       pur.cost AS cost
FROM purchases pur
LEFT JOIN breweries b ON pur.brewery_id = b.id
LEFT JOIN products p ON pur.product_id = p.id
accepted.description: One-row-per-purchase event enriched with brewery and product descriptive fields for easy consumption by reporting and aggregation layers. | Use for: Analyze purchase costs and volumes by brewery or product.; Time-series of purchases, e.g., monthly or per supplier.; Join with inventory or products_dim to reconcile receipts.

accepted.name: inventory_by_location_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT location_id AS location_id,
       product_id AS product_id,
       SUM(qty) AS qty_onhand,
       MIN(id) AS sample_inventory_id
FROM inventory
GROUP BY location_id, product_id
accepted.description: Current inventory quantities aggregated by location and product (one row per location_id+product_id). Useful to compute on-hand across locations and join to locations or products for dispatch/planning. | Use for: Compute stock-on-hand by location or product for replenishment.; Join to locations and products_dim to build picking lists.; Compare on-hand to product_minimums or monthly_budget.

accepted.name: orders_with_lines
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT ol.id AS id,
       ol.order_id AS order_id,
       o.customer_id AS customer_id,
       c.name AS name_customer,
       o.ordered AS ordered,
       o.delivery AS delivery,
       ol.product_id AS product_id,
       p.name AS name_product,
       ol.qty AS qty,
       ol.amount AS amount
FROM orderlines ol
LEFT JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.id
LEFT JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN products p ON ol.product_id = p.id
accepted.description: Denormalized order-line level detail: one row per orderline including order header and customer info. Useful for sales reporting, customer order histories and fulfillment analyses. | Use for: Order line level revenue and quantity analyses by customer, product, or date.; Build customer order histories or compute fulfillment KPIs.; Feed into picking/picking_list processes and reconcile with picking_line.

accepted.name: ticker_daily
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT symbol AS symbol,
       day AS day,
       AVG(price) AS price_avg
FROM ticker
GROUP BY symbol, day
accepted.description: Canonical daily ticker price per symbol and day. Aggregates in case of duplicates and exposes a simple price measure for time-series analyses or joins to stock. | Use for: Time-series stock price analysis and joins to stock for company-level reports.; Compute returns, moving averages, and compare with business events.

accepted.name: web_page_visit_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT app_id AS app_id,
       page_no AS page_no,
       date(visit_time) AS day,
       COUNT(*) AS visits
FROM web_page_visits
GROUP BY app_id, page_no, date(visit_time)
accepted.description: Counts of web page visits per app_id, page_no and day. Useful to analyze traffic trends, join to web_pages for friendly_url and compute daily metrics. | Use for: Daily traffic per page for engagement or capacity planning.; Join to web_pages to get friendly_url and to web_counter_hist for validation.

accepted.name: employees_hierarchy
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT id AS id,
       name AS name,
       title AS title,
       supervisor_id AS supervisor_id,
       id AS root_id,
       name AS root_name,
       0 AS depth,
       CAST(id AS TEXT) AS path
FROM employees
WHERE supervisor_id IS NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT e.id AS id,
       e.name AS name,
       e.title AS title,
       e.supervisor_id AS supervisor_id,
       h.root_id AS root_id,
       h.root_name AS root_name,
       h.depth + 1 AS depth,
       h.path || '>' || CAST(e.id AS TEXT) AS path
FROM employees e
JOIN employees_hierarchy h ON e.supervisor_id = h.id
accepted.description: Recursive employee reporting chain: each row is an employee-supervisor hop allowing construction of full reporting paths. Useful for org chart explorations, span-of-control, and manager-level rollups. | Use for: Build full reporting chains from top-level managers down.; Compute depth or path-based analyses like span-of-control.

accepted.name: web_devices_totals
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT day AS day,
       pc AS pc,
       tablet AS tablet,
       phone AS phone,
       (COALESCE(pc,0) + COALESCE(tablet,0) + COALESCE(phone,0)) AS total_devices
FROM web_devices
accepted.description: Normalized daily device totals and a derived total_devices measure. One row per day with device breakdown and total. Useful as canonical input for traffic or cross-day comparisons. | Use for: Daily device mix and totals for analytics dashboards.; Join to web_demographics or web_page_visits for deeper segmentation.

accepted.name: web_demographics_unpivot
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT day AS day,
       'M' AS letter,
       'tw' AS channel_shortcut,
       m_tw_cnt AS cnt,
       m_tw_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day AS day,
       'M' AS letter,
       'fb' AS channel_shortcut,
       m_fb_cnt AS cnt,
       m_fb_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day AS day,
       'F' AS letter,
       'tw' AS channel_shortcut,
       f_tw_cnt AS cnt,
       f_tw_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
UNION ALL
SELECT day AS day,
       'F' AS letter,
       'fb' AS channel_shortcut,
       f_fb_cnt AS cnt,
       f_fb_qty AS qty
FROM web_demographics
accepted.description: Unpivots denormalized web_demographics into one row per day + gender + channel with cnt and qty measures. Useful to filter by gender or channel without parsing column names and to aggregate across channels/genders. | Use for: Aggregate demographics by gender or channel over time.; Join to channels_dim or gender_dim (channel_shortcut to channels_dim.shortcut) after mapping.

accepted.name: latest_purchase_per_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT id AS id,
       purchased AS purchased,
       brewery_id AS brewery_id,
       product_id AS product_id,
       qty AS qty,
       cost AS cost,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased DESC, id DESC) AS purchase_rank
FROM purchases
accepted.description: Latest purchase event per product using purchased timestamp ordering. Exposes a rank so downstream queries can select latest (rank = 1). One row per purchase event with purchase_rank within product. | Use for: Find the most recent purchase for each product.; Compute supplier lead-times by comparing latest purchase to demand.
